note: Proposed NEW JFR events derived from gap analysis of -Xlog log sites that no existing JFR event covers. These events DO NOT exist in the JDK 26 oracle (196 events); they are candidates for upstream proposal. Scope of this analysis: -Xlog:trimnative*,gc*,gc+region*,gc+ergo*,gc+humongous*,stringdedup*=info (127 uncovered firing sites). Each 'replaces' entry cites the HotSpot source file + verbatim log format string the event would make recoverable via JFR. Field types follow the oracle convention (long for time/bytes/counters, int for ids, float/double for ratios, boolean/String). startTime/duration follow the standard JFR event contract. Status note (2026-08-18): JDK 26 (196 events) added jdk.StringDeduplication + jdk.FinalFieldMutation vs JDK 25 (194 events). JDK 27-dev master adds jdk.ShenandoahPromotionInformation. JDK-8365306 (NativeHeapTrim JFR, PR #26756, closed 2025-12): PR was blocked on ProcessSize umbrella design — narrow trim-only re-proposal recommended. G1 now has UseGCOverheadLimit (JDK-8212084, merged JDK 26, PR #27950) but no JFR event. JEP 521 Generational Shenandoah became production-ready in JDK 25. None of the other proposed events have upstream work in progress as of 2026-08-18. [Passes 1-7 history preserved in docs/research/README.md.] Critique pass 8 applied 2026-08-17 — EMISSION POINT AUDIT + FIELD CONSOLIDATION: (1) ZNMethodRegistration.tableRebuilt DROPPED — no source exists in ZStatNMethods::print(); would require new instrumentation; (2) PSAdaptiveSizePolicy: promotionRateEstimate, promotionRateLast DROPPED (derivable as promotedBytes/gcDistance); throughputGoal DROPPED (re-derived from GCTimeRatio, available from jdk.GCConfiguration); (3) G1CollectionSetCandidates.continueMixed DROPPED — from G1Policy::decide_on_concurrent_start_pause(), different call site from finalize_old_part(); (4) G1ConcurrentRefinementSweep and G1ConcurrentRefinementPolicy confirmed SEPARATE (different cadences — concurrent thread vs per-GC-pause thread); (5) ShenandoahCollectionDecision and ShenandoahReclaimProgress confirmed SEPARATE (start-of-cycle vs end-of-degenerated/full-GC); (6) ZGCTenuringThreshold and ShenandoahTenuringThreshold confirmed SEPARATE (different algorithms, different lifecycles); (7) ZDirectorRule redesign recommended: 22 mostly-null fields → per-tick summary event; see docs/research/event-consolidation.md; (8) ShenandoahMMU.report() path confirmed log_debug (not log_info) — isPeriodicSample path is debug-tier; (9) ShenandoahReclaimProgress simplification recommended: 12-field nullable event → 5-field simplified upstream version (freePercent, goodProgress, failedDimension, badProgressCount); (10) G1HeapResize fires on EVERY young GC even when resizeBytes=0 — consider gating JFR emission on resizeBytes != 0. Critique pass 9 applied 2026-08-18 — SCHEMA CLEANUP + REDUNDANCY AUDIT: (1) GCOverheadLimitExceeded.consecutiveViolations REMOVED — always equals GCOverheadLimitThreshold (develop flag, always 5 in production), zero information value; (2) PSAdaptiveSizePolicy.throughputEdenIncrease REPLACED with edenSizingBranch enum ('throughput_grow'|'pause_shrink'|'distance_grow'|'distance_shrink'|'unchanged') — non-null, captures branch label, raw delta derivable from jdk.PSHeapSummary; (3) ShenandoahReclaimProgress: badProgressCount + failedDimension added as simplified 5-field upstream version; 12-field full version preserved as reference; (4) ZGCTenuringThreshold status updated to REDESIGN FIRST — jdk.ZYoungGarbageCollection already has tenuringThreshold, preferred approach is adding tenuringThresholdReason field to existing event; (5) ShenandoahCollectionDecision.decision field marked RECOMMENDED TO DROP for initial proposal — always 'normal' at service_concurrent_normal_cycle() emission point.

proposed.label: Shenandoah Card Statistics
proposed.status: BLOCKED — source code gate. The ShenandoahCardStats::log() method is wrapped in #ifndef PRODUCT (confirmed: shenandoahCardStats.cpp lines 31-42). This means the data is NOT available in production JVM builds. A JFR event proposal would need to FIRST move the data collection out of the #ifndef PRODUCT guard into product code. This is a prerequisite code change, not just an event proposal. Until that upstream change is made, this event cannot fire in production. The data itself (dirty/clean card distribution, alternation count) remains valuable for generational Shenandoah observability.
proposed.rationale: Shenandoah generational (only, JEP 521 production-ready in JDK 25) remembered-set card scanning emits cumulative dirty/clean card statistics per GC cycle with no JFR event. IMPORTANT: the log() method is wrapped in #ifndef PRODUCT (confirmed from source: lines 31-42 in shenandoahCardStats.cpp) — this event would only fire in debug/fastdebug builds unless the JFR emission point is moved to a product-build path. Log tag is gc,remset (NOT gc or gc,ergo). Log level is log_info (NOT log_debug). The per-worker stats are gated behind ShenandoahEnableCardStats (non-product); this event emits only the cumulative aggregate. dirtyScannedObjects maps to _dirty_scan_obj_cnt — the count of heap objects visited as a result of dirty card scans (distinct from dirtyCards = card-table slot count). maxConsecutiveDirtyCards reflects card-table clustering that affects scan efficiency. _alternation_cnt confirmed as exact field name in shenandoahCardStats.hpp.

proposed.label: Shenandoah Minimum Mutator Utilization
proposed.rationale: Shenandoah's MMU tracker prints GC utilization (GCU) and mutator utilization (MU) per completed phase with no JFR analogue. NOT redundant with jdk.G1MMU: G1MMU measures pause-time compliance within a fixed time-slice window (gcTime vs pauseTarget in ms); ShenandoahMMU measures GCU%/MU% utilization fractions over the entire phase window — semantically different metrics answering different questions. Low muPercent directly indicates mutator starvation. Emission points: (1) update_utilization() at end of each GC cycle (log_info(gc,ergo)) — primary anchor; (2) record_old_marking_increment() for old marking increments (log_info(gc,ergo)); (3) report() periodic sample called from ShenandoahMmuTask::task() at GCPauseIntervalMillis interval — BUT report() is log_debug(gc), not log_info. PASS 8 NOTE: the isPeriodicSample=true path corresponds to log_debug(gc) — it is a debug-tier data point. isPeriodicSample boolean distinguishes end-of-cycle (log_info) from periodic sample (log_debug). gcId from _most_recent_gcid is needed for GC event correlation.

proposed.label: Shenandoah Reclaim Progress
proposed.rationale: shenandoahMetrics.cpp's is_good_progress() evaluates four independent dimensions after each cycle. Emission point: called from ShenandoahDegenGC::op_final_roots() and ShenandoahFullGC::op_gc() — fires ONLY after degenerated or full GCs, NOT after normal concurrent cycles. IMPORTANT early-exit semantics: the function returns on the FIRST dimension that passes (or after free-space fails) — not all 4 dimensions are logged every cycle. Fields for dimensions 2-4 are NULLABLE. Fragmentation values are fractions (0.0-1.0) in source; stored as percentage (0.0-100.0) here for usability. freeNeeded = (softMaxCapacity/100) * ShenandoahCriticalFreeThreshold (bytes). goodProgress=false in any dimension signals risk of degenerated GC fallback. UPSTREAM DESIGN: use the simplified 5-field version (freePercent, goodProgress, failedDimension, badProgressCount — plus startTime) for initial upstream submission. The 12-field nullable design below will face pushback. badProgressCount is the most actionable field: value >= 2 (CONSECUTIVE_BAD_DEGEN_PROGRESS_THRESHOLD) means Full GC fires on the next failure. failedDimension discriminates 'free_space' (hard gate failed — OOM risk) from 'all_secondary' (free passed but GC made no measurable progress). The 12 detailed fields are preserved below as a full-version reference but are NOT recommended for the initial proposal.

proposed.label: ZGC NMethod Registration
proposed.rationale: ZGC requires all nmethods to have load barriers patched (registered). Field semantics from ZNMethodTable.cpp: registeredNMethods = _nregistered (current live count); staleNMethodSlots = _nunregistered (entries unregistered but not yet pruned — zombie entries pending table rebuild, NOT a cumulative total). Emission point: ZStatNMethods::print() called from ZStatPhaseGeneration::register_end() — fires once per ZGC generation collection. PASS 8 CHANGE: tableRebuilt field DROPPED — no per-cycle tableRebuilt boolean exists in ZStatNMethods::print(); would require new instrumentation. Production validation: low — no external evidence found that nmethod table overhead is a common production problem. Recommend de-prioritizing.

proposed.label: GC Overhead Limit Exceeded
proposed.logLevelNote: REDESIGNED (pass 7): The per-GC counter update logs ('GC Overhead Limit: GC Time %f...') are log_debug(gc) — NOT in scope. Only the OOM-throw path ('GC Overhead Limit exceeded too often') is log_info(gc). Event redesigned to fire ONCE at the OOM throw point only, with accumulated context. The per-GC counter data (gcTimePercent, freeSpacePercent) must be captured in the JFR event at the OOM throw site (where the current values are accessible via _policy->analytics() / _size_policy) not from the debug log.
proposed.rationale: Fires immediately before the JVM throws OutOfMemoryError: GC Overhead Limit exceeded. Now implemented in both G1 (JDK-8212084, merged JDK 26 PR #27950) and Parallel GC — but no JFR event was added. EVENT SCOPE (pass 7): fires ONLY at the OOM throw point (satisfy_failed_allocation paths where gc_overhead_limit_exceeded() returns true), NOT per-GC-cycle. At the throw site, all relevant context is still accessible: g1CollectedHeap.cpp:1110 log_info(gc)('GC Overhead Limit exceeded too often (%zu)') and parallelScavengeHeap.cpp:507 log_info(gc)('GC Overhead Limit exceeded too often (%zu)'). The per-GC diagnostic values (gcTimePercent, freeSpace) must be read from GC analytics at the throw site, not from the debug counter-update log. gcId is GCId::peek() — last completed GC id (approximate).

proposed.label: Native Heap Trim
proposed.rationale: The JVM periodically calls malloc_trim/madvise to return RSS to the OS (NativeHeapTrimmer thread, -XX:TrimNativeHeapInterval). Especially valuable on containerised deployments. JDK-8365306 (PR #26756) was closed 2025-12 — the NativeHeapTrim event itself was not objected to; a narrow trim-only re-proposal is recommended. deltaBytes is SIGNED: afterBytes - beforeBytes (negative = RSS reduced, positive = RSS grew). trimCount = _num_trims_performed (uint64_t, first = 1). detailsAvailable=false when /proc/self/status unavailable. IMPLEMENTATION CONSTRAINT (pass 7): RSS data (sc.before/sc.after) is collected at trimNativeHeap.cpp:141 ONLY when logging is enabled ('const bool logging_enabled = lt.is_enabled()'). A JFR event implementation must call os::trim_native_heap() with a non-null SizingCollection* unconditionally (decoupled from log level), or restructure the call. This is a minor code change but must be addressed in the upstream proposal. Note: jdk.ResidentSetSize already exists in JFR (confirmed in JDK 27 master) but tracks instantaneous RSS; NativeHeapTrim captures the DELTA from a deliberate trim operation — complementary, not redundant.

proposed.label: G1 Collection Set Candidates
proposed.logLevelNote: All select_candidates_from_marking/retained log sites are log_debug(gc,ergo,cset). JFR event would expose G1 mixed-GC selection reasoning in production for the first time.
proposed.rationale: G1's mixed-GC region selection reasoning is entirely invisible in JFR today. jdk.EvacuationInformation records the outcome (regions evacuated, bytes); this event records the DECISION: how many candidates were available, how many selected, whether time budget was exceeded, and why mixed GCs stopped. There are TWO separate candidate paths: (1) MARKING candidates — regions identified by concurrent marking as high-garbage; (2) RETAINED candidates — regions from previous cycles that were deferred. Both paths have equivalent log structures and should be covered by a single event with a candidateType discriminator. Emission point: G1CollectionSet::finalize_old_part() called from finalize_initial_collection_set() during young GC pause preparation. Fires twice per mixed GC (once Marking, once Retained); zero times during non-mixed pauses. IMPORTANT corrections from source audit: (1) proposed 'predictedTimeExceeded' boolean does not exist as a variable — source has 'Added %u ... although the predicted time was too high' (count of over-budget regions added). (2) 'groups' (card-set groups, not region count) is logged separately and adds context. (3) predicted initial/optional times and optional threshold are available from the Finish log. PASS 8 CHANGE: continueMixed DROPPED — comes from G1Policy::decide_on_concurrent_start_pause(), a different call site from the candidate selection functions; attaching it to this event would require state from a different code location. No existing event covers this; jdk.G1AdaptiveIHOP/jdk.G1BasicIHOP cover IHOP (marking trigger), not collection-set selection. PRIORITY DOWNGRADED (pass 7): all log sites are log_debug(gc,ergo,cset).

proposed.logLevelNote: log_resize() is log_debug(gc,ergo,heap) — requires -Xlog:gc+ergo+heap=debug. JFR event would expose heap resize drivers (CPU usage vs thresholds) in production for the first time.
proposed.rationale: G1's adaptive heap resize (expand/shrink) is driven by CPU-usage feedback in g1HeapSizingPolicy.cpp. The size delta is computable from jdk.G1HeapSummary before/after, but the DRIVERS (short/long-term GC-CPU-usage %, thresholds, scale factor, which trigger fired) are in no existing event — these are the actual tuning signal for G1ExpandByPercent / GCTimeRatio. (5) The expand log has lowerThreshold/upperThreshold/gcCpuUsageTarget — missing from original proposal. direction = expand (bool in source, tristate derivable from expand + resize_bytes==0). CONFIRMED medium (pass 7): log_debug(gc,ergo,heap) consistent with prior priority.

proposed.label: ZGC Director Rule Evaluation
proposed.logLevelNote: ALL ZDirector rule log sites are log_debug(gc,director) — requires -Xlog:gc+director=debug. A JFR event would expose ZGC collection trigger reasoning in production for the first time.
proposed.rationale: ZGC's director evaluates rules to decide whether to trigger GC. Emission point: all rule functions called from make_minor_gc_decision() and make_major_gc_decision() → start_gc() → director tick loop. Early-exit: at most ONE Minor rule and ONE Major rule fire per tick. Cadence: every director tick (~1s). IMPORTANT design notes: (1) Early-exit: make_minor/major_gc_decision return on first triggered rule — at most one Minor and one Major rule fires per cycle. (2) rule_minor_allocation_rate_static (UseDynamicNumberOfGCThreads=false) is a separate variant with NO gcCPUTime/gcWorkers/allocRateVariancePct. (3) Proactive rule has TWO mutually exclusive branches (enabled vs not-yet-enabled). (4) rule_major_allocation_rate is an ESCALATION rule from start_gc(), not make_major_gc_decision(). (5) Timer rule applies to both generations. (6) High Usage log has freePercent. Generation values 'Young'/'Old' align with JFR convention. PASS 8 REDESIGN RECOMMENDED: this event has 22 fields but each rule populates only 3-5. Consider redesigning as a per-tick summary event: single 'jdk.ZDirectorStats' with generation, triggeredMinorRule (String, null if no GC triggered), triggeredMajorRule (String, null), timeUntilMinorOOM, minorFreeBytes, majorFreePercent — 6 fields instead of 22. The current per-rule per-field design is preserved here for completeness but will likely face upstream pushback on sparseness. PRIORITY DOWNGRADED (pass 7): ALL rule log sites confirmed log_debug(gc,director) — no log_info anywhere in zDirector.cpp.

proposed.label: ZGC Tenuring Threshold Selection
proposed.status: REDESIGN FIRST — jdk.ZYoungGarbageCollection already has a tenuringThreshold field (confirmed in metadata.xml). The preferred upstream approach is to add a tenuringThresholdReason field (String: 'Promote All' | 'ZTenuringThreshold' | 'Computed') to the existing jdk.ZYoungGarbageCollection event rather than creating a new standalone event. This is a smaller diff, avoids duplicating the threshold value, and will receive less friction. Only propose the standalone event if timing granularity (fires earlier, at select_relocation_set() rather than collection end) is a distinct requirement. See verdict in jfr-event-proposals.md.
proposed.rationale: ZGC generational mode computes a tenuring threshold each young collection via ZGenerationYoung::select_tenuring_threshold(). The function logs at log_info(gc, reloc) with 'Using tenuring threshold: %d (%s)' — production code, no JFR coverage. The reason field identifies three selection paths: 'Promote All' (forced, via promote_all flag), 'ZTenuringThreshold' (user-pinned via -XX:ZTenuringThreshold), or 'Computed' (dynamic algorithm using life decay factor × log residency). The computed algorithm in compute_tenuring_threshold() uses: young_life_decay_factor (reciprocal of average ratio between consecutive age cohorts — higher = more generational = promote later), allocated_garbage_ratio (allocation pressure — high = prefer promoting to help YC keep up), and young_log_residency (heap fraction occupied by young gen — small fraction = promote later). The computed value is clamped between 1 and min(last_populated_age+1, MaxTenuringThreshold). Note: the debug-level diagnostic fields (allocatedGarbageRatio, youngLogResidency, lifeDecayFactor logged at log_debug) are intentionally NOT included in this event — only the info-level result. ZUncommit already exists as jdk.ZUncommit (metadata.xml:1248, EventZUncommit::commit() in update_statistics()).

proposed.label: Shenandoah Tenuring Threshold Adjustment
proposed.rationale: Shenandoah generational mode tracks object ages and dynamically adjusts the tenuring threshold (the age at which young objects are promoted to old generation). shenandoahAgeCensus.cpp emits a log_info(gc, age) line whenever the threshold changes. This is analogous to jdk.TenuringDistribution (which exists for G1/Parallel) but for Shenandoah's generational mode — and captures THRESHOLD CHANGES (not per-age-bucket sizes). ShenandoahGenerationalMinTenuringAge and ShenandoahGenerationalMaxTenuringAge bound the range. Note: jdk.TenuringDistribution already covers G1 and Parallel GC for per-bucket sizes; this event is Shenandoah-specific and covers only the computed threshold value, not the full age histogram (which would require a separate event). Production value: repeated threshold decreases (toward minTenuringAge) indicate young gen collection pressure; threshold increases (toward maxTenuringAge) indicate stable survivor space usage.
